### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8021368beaa6358fdd26c752ebf8f1cf8058861c` — the merge of head `3203683dc66c57c0425d74ab484b534ee7e07e4a` into base `e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8021368beaa6358fdd26c752ebf8f1cf8058861c && git checkout 8021368beaa6358fdd26c752ebf8f1cf8058861c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a 3203683dc66c57c0425d74ab484b534ee7e07e4a && git checkout -B drift-repro e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a && git merge --no-ff 3203683dc66c57c0425d74ab484b534ee7e07e4a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e728d7a122fd68e1a3b1a4df27b07b4b13b2295a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5cee1bbe5f70167bffccb2e2c0004fcb92d80e97`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/run-dropped-fields.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts

Widened, read and graded because the brief asked: the four test files, `.changeset/32861-flow-answer-dropped-fields.md`, and the regenerated `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`. Read at this head, never reviewed: `builtin/map-node.ts`, `run-history.ts`, `suspended-run-store.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts`, and spec `data/data-engine.zod.ts`, `automation/execution.zod.ts`, `api/protocol.zod.ts`.

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-13T04:12Z: 32 success, 10 skipped, 24 in_progress (Test Core 1 to 8, Test UI 1 to 16), 0 failed. Every type-check, lint, build, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` run is green. The test shards had not concluded, so "every check green" is the seat's to re-read before queueing.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data.droppedFields` is a widening: right.** It is `z.array(DroppedFieldsEventSchema).optional()` on a strip-mode object, so every payload accepted before is still accepted. The one theoretical exception is a payload that already carried a top-level `droppedFields` of another shape, which the schema used to strip silently. No producer on `main` emits one; the step's `output.droppedFields` sits inside `z.unknown()`. The doors relay without parsing, so nothing is refused at run time.
2. **`AutomationResult.droppedFields?` is a widening: right.** `TriggerFlowDataMatchesContract` in `automation-api.zod.test.ts` binds schema and contract member for member. An `IAutomationService` implementer need not set it.
3. **`NodeExecutionResult.droppedFields?` and `StepLogEntry.droppedFields?` are widenings: right.** The PR body calls them service-internal. They are on the exported executor contract and on the persisted step log; the same declaration and the service-automation changeset entry cover them. The wire consequence is nit N2.
4. **Omit-when-empty: right.** `withDroppedFields` returns an empty object unless the fold found an event with at least one field. It is pinned by `'droppedFields' in res === false` at the engine, at both action entrances and on the real kernel.
5. **Refused, failed, paused, never-dispatched and skip exits carry none: right.** `finishRefusedRun`, both `status: 'failed'` exits, the exhausted-retry exit, the paused returns and the two skip returns are untouched.
6. **Vocabulary: none new, right.** The element is the existing `DroppedFieldsEventSchema`. `CreateDataResponse`, `UpdateDataResponse`, `CreateManyDataResponse`, the batch results and the import row result already carry it under the same member name. One event per object and reason with the field union is the convention `CreateManyDataResponse.droppedFields` already states.
7. **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** Nothing a metadata author can write changes, and no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation`: right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says the level follows the kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces that a declared `none` grades every entry `patch` and moves no authorable baseline. `Check Changeset` is green.
- **Declaration lines: identical.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial and the same in the PR body and the changeset.
- **`@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/verify`: no entry owed.** The diff adds only test files there.
- **should-fix (changeset prose) P1: the changeset names a route that does not exist.** It lists `POST /api/v1/data/:object/:id/actions/:action` as a door that relays the answer. `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts` states that no action-invoke route exists in the data family and that its absence is deliberate (#7680). The second spelling the dispatcher mounts is `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action/:recordId` (`packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`). The changeset ships as CHANGELOG.md.
- **should-fix (changeset prose) P2: the subflow sentence is unconditional and the code is not.** "a `subflow` child's drops ride up onto its parent's answer" holds only for a child that completes without pausing. The PR body says so; the changeset does not. See S1.
- **nit (changeset prose): the doors list omits the resume door.** `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/runs/:runId/resume` and the MCP `resume_run` tool are where "a drop before a pause" is delivered.
- A fix confined to the changeset does not move a reviewed file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (close the card or keep `Part of`): A.** The card's Expected is the toast. `Part of #32861` is right. #33009 (`domain:ui`) is filed, blocked by this PR, and #32861 closes when it lands.
- **Console half split: accepted.** Triage comment 6837363004 allowed the split when the console needs more than rendering the answer. The three reasons given are reader-side and none is refuted by the tree.
- **Out-of-scope finding "carrier: none" (a paused subflow child does not roll up): escalated, it needs a carrier.** "No public door was measured reaching it" is a not-measured. By reading, the delegated leg is the one a screen flow takes: the resume route relays `resume()` whole, and `run-resume.ts` continues the parent with the child's output and summary only. The same gap exists for every `map` item, which the dev report does not mention. See S1.
- **NOT MEASURED gate (`check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`): answered by CI.** The step runs in `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, which is green on this head.
- **First-run red on `check:test-source-alias`: answered.** `5cee1bbe` adds the collection-time imports and the lint jobs are green on this head.
- **PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`:** no off-relay login to name.
- **`main` moved seven commits past the merge base, to `ee9ad834`.** None touches a path of this diff. #32952 among them narrows the runtime object write doors only; the verify fixture boots a code stack.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix: none.**

**What holds, read in the tree**

- **`automation-api.zod.ts`:** the member reuses the engine's schema, as the record-save answers do. The describe is true of the run's own write steps sentence by sentence, including `stored_expression` ("did not store" covers a value replaced by the computed one). The first consumer's parser, `isWireDroppedFieldsEntry` in `ui/packages/data-objectstack`, reads this entry shape.
- **`automation-service.ts`:** the jsdoc matches the fold (one event per object and reason, first-seen order, absent and never an empty array).
- **`run-dropped-fields.ts`:** the fold copies `fields`, so no step or child array is mutated. Map insertion order gives first-seen order. It dedupes by object, reason and field, so a loop, a `try_catch` retry or a re-entered node cannot double count.
- **`engine.ts`, `dag-traversal.ts`, `run-resume.ts`:** the only three `status: 'completed'` sites in the package each carry the spread. There is no fourth terminal-success exit.
- **Pause and resume:** `resumeInternal` folds `run.steps`, the array the pause persisted. `ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore` writes `JSON.stringify(run.steps)` whole and reads it back unprojected, so a pre-pause drop survives a durable pause.
- **`crud-nodes.ts`:** the events are the ones the node already collected; `output.droppedFields` and `warnings` are byte-unchanged.
- **`subflow-node.ts`:** a child that completed hands up its own fold. A failed or refused child has none. The child's steps live in the child's log, so the parent cannot count them twice.
- **Accepted scenario (card Work 1 and 3, the #32666 shape):** pinned at the engine, at both action entrances with a scripted service, and on the real kernel through `actions.run` (answer names `status`, record stays `draft`, `note` lands). The reported ablation is consistent with the code: the four cases that read an exit go red; the two fold cases and the drop-nothing case do not.

**should-fix S1 (both hits, `subflow-node.ts`): delegation is undeclared and uneven.**
- The same answer's `summary` credits a child run's writes from a `subflow` and from each `map` item, on the synchronous leg and on both resumed legs (`creditChildRun`).
- `droppedFields` rolls up only from a `subflow` child that completes without pausing. `builtin/map-node.ts` never reads `child.droppedFields`. The delegated resume leg and `bubbleToParent` carry output and summary only.
- So a parent whose `map` items each drop `status` answers `summary.acted: N` with no `droppedFields`.
- The jsdoc says "the run's own write steps", which the subflow roll-up already exceeds. Neither published sentence tells a reader that absence is not proof for a delegated write.
- Smallest fix here: one sentence on both hits, and the regenerated mdx, stating the rule as built. A `subflow` child that completes without pausing rolls up; a child that paused, and a `map` item's run, do not.
- Then a server-lane card for the roll-up itself (the map node's completion exit and `creditChildRun`'s two callers). Doing the roll-up in this PR is the alternative.
- Until then #33009's reader must not treat an absent member as "nothing was dropped" for those shapes.

**should-fix S2 (pin): the retried-attempt exit is unpinned.**
- None of the seven cases declares `errorHandling.strategy: 'retry'`.
- The ablation cut the shared helper, which reds all three exits together, so it cannot show per-exit coverage.
- Deleting the spread in `executeWithoutRetry` leaves every test green. That file's own comments count seven drifts of this method from `execute()`.
- One case closes it: a flow under `strategy: 'retry'` whose first attempt fails and whose second completes with a drop.

**nit N1: the fold runs after `recordLog('completed')`, inside the `try` whose `catch` reads any throw as a node failure (the #16274 and #15944 class).**
- It cannot throw on well-typed events, and both in-tree producers are well-typed.
- A host-registered executor returning a malformed `droppedFields` would turn a completed run into a failed or retried one.
- Harden in the commit that moves the head for S1 or S2, or carry it on the follow-up card.

**nit N2: the step-log member reaches a published wire undeclared.**
- `steps[].droppedFields` is persisted in run history and served verbatim by `GET /automation/:name/runs/:runId` and the runs list.
- `ExecutionStepLogSchema` declares neither it nor `warnings`; that drift predates this PR (#3407).
- Follow-up card: declare both, or project them out.

**nit N3: "Set on a terminal success only" can be read to include `status: 'refused'`, which answers `success: true`.** The code sets the member on a completed run only. `successMessage` uses the same phrase with the same exclusion, so this is an accepted deviation.

**nit N4: the union reading is unstated.** A name means at least one write dropped it, not every write. `CreateManyDataResponse.droppedFields` says so in its describe; this one does not. Add it if the describe is touched for S1.

**nit N5: the failure-arm copy in `executeNode` is unreachable today.** No executor returns `droppedFields` beside `success: false`. Harmless symmetry with `warnings`.

**nit N6: the pause pin runs on `InMemorySuspendedRunStore` only.** The durable round trip holds by reading and is unpinned.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3203683dc66c57c0425d74ab484b534ee7e07e4a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/run-dropped-fields.test.ts, .changeset/32861-flow-answer-dropped-fields.md, content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx

Delta review of record 6843734657 (PASS on `5cee1bbe`, with should-fix S1, S2, P1 and P2 open). The head moved by three linear commits (`db40c4a8`, `cca51fda`, `3203683d`) with no merge of `main`; the merge base is still `04c35f09`. The five files on the Scope line are the whole delta. Read at this head, never reviewed: `builtin/subflow-node.ts`, `builtin/map-node.ts`, `run-resume.ts`, `engine.ts` (`bubbleToParent`, `retryExecution`), `dag-traversal.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs`.

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-13T04:56Z: 26 success, 12 skipped, 31 in_progress, 0 failed.
- Green: every lint job (including `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which runs `pnpm check:doc-authoring`, and `Lint · docs & code guards`), `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.
- Not concluded: Test Core 1 to 8, Test UI 1 to 16, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, and the workspace, UI, consumer-gates and debt-ledger type checks.
- The shard that runs the new retry pin is among those still running, so its green rests on the dev report (8 of 8) until the seat re-reads.

Check-runs on the round-1 head `5cee1bbe`, read 2026-11-13T04:54Z: all concluded, 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. The 24 shards that record 6843734657 left in progress are answered green.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta changes no accept set and no type.** The `automation-api.zod.ts` hunk is one `//` comment and the describe string; `z.array(DroppedFieldsEventSchema).optional()` is untouched. The `automation-service.ts` hunk is jsdoc only; the member's type is untouched.
- **All seven judgments of 6843734657 carry unchanged:** widening on schema and contract, the two service-automation members, omit-when-empty, nothing on refused, failed or paused exits, no new vocabulary, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **The describe string is published text** (JSON Schema description and the reference page). The change documents the same accept set; it neither widens nor narrows it.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on both packages: still right.** The delta publishes prose only. The declaration lines are unchanged in the changeset and identical in the replaced PR body. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- **P1 closed.** The data-family route is gone from the changeset and from the tree. The second door now named, `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action/:recordId`, is mounted in `dispatcher-plugin.ts` and has a row in `route-ledger.ts`.
- **P2 closed.** The changeset now says a `subflow` child that completes without pausing rolls up, and that a child that paused and a `map` item's run do not yet (#33019). That is the code; see ④.
- **Doors nit closed.** The changeset adds `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/runs/:runId/resume` and the MCP `resume_run` tool. Both relay the engine's answer: the REST door ends `deps.success(result)`, and `resume_run` answers it under `result`, as `run_action` does. The trigger and resume routes both have rows in `route-ledger.ts`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Seat rulings 6843826357 item 2: all four executed in this push.** Dev report 6844392691 carries no open question.
- **Declared deviation (the card id is not inside the describe): accepted.**
  - The describe says "do not yet" and #33019 sits in the adjacent `//` comment; the jsdoc and the changeset keep the id.
  - `pnpm check:doc-authoring` refuses an issue id in describe prose, because that string projects into the reference page and the published schema. `protocol.zod.ts` states the same rule for `CreateManyDataResponse`.
  - The gate is green on this head.
- **Carriers verified by reading.**
  - #33019 (`domain:server`, open): the map exit, both callers of `creditChildRun`, and N1's fold hardening.
  - #33020 (`domain:spec`, open): N2.
  - #33009: the console half.
  - N3, N5 and N6 stand as accepted by the seat.
- **Replaced PR body:** `Part of #32861`, the two declaration lines, the 8-case count and the delegated rule agree with the tree. It still labels the two service-automation members service-internal; item 3 of ① in 6843734657 and #33020 are the correction of record.
- **`main` is now `e728d7a1`.** Since round 1 it gained #32987, which changes `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` in the route-declaration resolution for a refused read. `dispatchFlowAction` is not touched and no path of this PR is touched. The merged tree is the queue's to run.
- **PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`:** no off-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix: none. should-fix: none.**

**S1 closed. Each new sentence on the two hits is true of the code.**

- **"a field named means at least one write dropped it, not every write"** (describe, jsdoc, changeset): true. `dropEventsOf` unions `fields` across steps under one object-and-reason key. This also closes N4.
- **"a `subflow` child that completes without pausing rolls its drops up"** (describe "here", jsdoc "onto this answer"): true.
  - `subflow-node.ts` puts a completed child's `droppedFields` on the parent's step, and the parent's fold reads it.
  - This holds when the parent itself pauses later, because the step is persisted.
  - A failed or refused child's answer carries none.
- **"a child that paused, and a `map` item's run, do not yet"**: true.
  - The delegated resume leg and `bubbleToParent` hand the parent the child's output and summary only.
  - `map-node.ts` never reads the member, on its synchronous exit or its paused one.
- **"an absent member is not proof that a delegated write dropped nothing"**: true. The converse it leaves standing also holds: the only built-in nodes that write records are `create_record` and `update_record`, and both report.
- **"unlike {@link summary}, which credits all three"** (jsdoc): true.
  - The subflow step's rolled metrics credit a child that completed.
  - `creditChildRun` credits a paused child on the delegated leg; on the up-bubble, `bubbleToParent` passes the child's summary into the parent's resume.
  - `map-node.ts` sums each item's summary, and a paused item is credited by the same `creditChildRun`.
- The jsdoc's earlier "the run's own write steps" now reads with the delegated paragraph that follows it. The two are consistent.
- The regenerated mdx row equals the describe string character for character and carries no card id.

**S2 closed.**

- The new case runs under `errorHandling: { strategy: 'retry', maxRetries: 1, backoffMs: 0 }`.
- Attempt 1 fails at the `flaky` node inside `execute()`, so `execute()`'s own completion exit is never reached. `retryExecution` returns attempt 2's result from `executeWithoutRetry`.
- So `res.droppedFields` can only come from the spread in `dag-traversal.ts`. `expect(attempts).toBe(2)` holds that the ladder ran.
- The reported single-exit ablation (1 failed, 7 passed of 8, the retry case alone red) is what the code predicts. The restored blob `aca7bf1a` is this head's blob for `dag-traversal.ts`.
- The same `errorHandling` block is already used in `end-node-refused-outcome.test.ts`.

**The files the delta leaves untouched stand as reviewed.**

- Blob ids are equal between `5cee1bbe` and this head for `run-dropped-fields.ts`, `engine.ts`, `dag-traversal.ts`, `run-resume.ts`, `builtin/crud-nodes.ts`, `builtin/subflow-node.ts`, and for `builtin/map-node.ts`, which the new sentences cite.
- The three other test files are byte-identical too.
- Every check on `5cee1bbe` has since concluded green.

**nit (new, pin): the retry case cannot tell attempt 2's drop from attempt 1's.** Both attempts drop the same field, while the title says "from the attempt that completed". The exit is what S2 asked to pin and it is pinned. Accepted as written.
